value.text: A master's graduate can apply for a 3-year post-graduation work permit (PGWP), even if the programme was under 2 years, if it lasted at least 8 months and all other requirements are met.
value.clock_note: The permit cannot run past the expiry date of your passport.

proposals.evidence_snippet: You can apply for a 3-year PGWP, even if your master’s program was less than 2 years, as long as your program was at least 8 months (or 900 hours for Quebec programs) and you meet all other eligibility requirements
proposals.notes: IRCC page 'About the PGWP'. Snippet lines are joined from consecutive list lines on the page.

value.text: After graduating in Germany you can apply for a residence permit for jobseekers, issued for up to 18 months, to look for qualified employment.
value.clock_note: You can then convert it into a work visa for qualified professionals or an EU Blue Card once you find a suitable job.

proposals.evidence_snippet: you must apply for a residence permit for jobseekers (go to “Staying in Germany after graduation”). It is issued for up to 18 months as a means of finding qualified employment.
proposals.notes: DAAD (official German academic exchange service). The Make it in Germany portal sits behind a bot challenge so it was not read.
